answer: A proof-of-space protocol prevents Sybil attacks by requiring agents to allocate disk space formatted with a verifiable cipher. Verifiers audit presence through random sector queries requiring an immediate data echo. An attacker forging identities incurs a verifiable hardware cost, dedicating physical storage per persona. Each plot acts as an unforgeable pearl of committed capacity. A key limitation is that perpetual audits induce disk wear and marginalize storage-poor nodes.
